findings.evidence: `def singletSector [DecidableEq Flavor] : Submodule R …` (l.113) alongside `def nonSinglet : Submodule R … := LinearMap.ker singletGluon` (l.175); docstring l.54 "`Species.singletSector`, `Species.nonSinglet`: the two sectors".
findings.fix: Rename `nonSinglet` to `nonSingletSector`, propagating to `mem_nonSingletSector`, `single_quark_sub_single_antiquark_mem_nonSingletSector`, `single_quark_add_single_antiquark_sub_…_mem_nonSingletSector`, `flavorBlindMatrix_mulVec_mem_nonSingletSector`, `…_of_mem_nonSingletSector`, `finrank_nonSingletSector`, `isCompl_singletSector_nonSingletSector`. `singletSector` cannot drop its suffix since `singlet` is already the functional (line 136).
findings.issue: The two parallel submodules of the same decomposition are named inconsistently: `singletSector` (line 113) vs `nonSinglet` (line 175), even though the module docstring calls both "the two sectors" (line 54) and `isCompl_singletSector_nonSinglet` (line 204) pairs them. Bare `nonSinglet` also reads like a predicate on vectors rather than a `Submodule`.

findings.evidence: l.397-398 `theorem flavorBlindMatrix_mulVec_of_mem_nonSinglet … : flavorBlindMatrix qq qg gq gg *ᵥ v = qq • v`; l.413-414 `theorem flavorBlindMatrix_mulVec_mem_nonSinglet … : flavorBlindMatrix qq qg gq gg *ᵥ v ∈ nonSinglet`.
findings.fix: Rename the equality lemma to `flavorBlindMatrix_mulVec_eq_smul_of_mem_nonSinglet`, keeping `flavorBlindMatrix_mulVec_mem_nonSinglet` for the invariance statement; update the two internal uses at l.409–410 and l.415 and the docstring entry at l.62–64.
findings.issue: `flavorBlindMatrix_mulVec_of_mem_nonSinglet` (conclusion `P *ᵥ v = qq • v`, l.398) and `flavorBlindMatrix_mulVec_mem_nonSinglet` (conclusion `P *ᵥ v ∈ nonSinglet`, l.414) differ only by `of_` yet state different results; the first name describes only the LHS and omits the equality it proves, so neither name lets a reader predict which is which.

findings.evidence: l.195-197; naming conventions: "the name of theorem simply describes the conclusion" and "When an operation is written as infix, the theorem names follow suit".
findings.fix: Spell out both operands, e.g. `single_quark_add_single_antiquark_sub_single_quark_add_single_antiquark_mem_nonSinglet`, so the `_`-separated parts track the expression as the convention requires.
findings.issue: `single_quark_add_single_antiquark_sub_mem_nonSinglet` truncates the expression it names: the statement is `(single (quark i) + single (antiquark i)) - (single (quark j) + single (antiquark j))`, but the name ends with a dangling `sub` and so reads as a subtraction with no right operand — it does not determine the statement, unlike the adjacent `single_quark_sub_single_antiquark_mem_nonSinglet` (l.190), which spells its expression out in full.

summary: Names are mostly descriptive and conclusion-first, but the two halves of the decomposition are named asymmetrically (`singletSector` vs `nonSinglet`), one pair of lemmas differs only by `of_` while asserting different conclusions, and one lemma name truncates the expression it is about. No notation is introduced.
